value.text:
Technical University of Kenya (TU-K) is a public university in Nairobi, Kenya. Its institutional history includes several distinct phases: Kenya Technical Institute in 1956, Kenya Polytechnic in 1961, and Kenya Polytechnic University College in 2007. The university grew out of Kenya Polytechnic, which had developed from the Kenya Technical Institute to provide diploma training and prepare middle-level personnel. TU-K received its university charter in January 2013 from then-president Mwai Kibaki. Its motto is “Education and Training for the Real World.”

The university college admitted its first cohort of degree students in January 2009. In July that year, the University of Nairobi Senate approved an initial group of programmes in electrical and electronic engineering, comprising Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Technology and Diploma in Technology courses. The programmes were designed for five, four and three years of study respectively. The university offers technical and vocational education alongside degree programmes, including DipTech, BTech, BPhil, BEng and BSc. Its listed academic structure comprises the Faculty of Engineering and Built Environment, Faculty of Applied Science and Technology, and Faculty of Social Sciences and Technology. Their schools cover engineering, architecture, computing, health and biological sciences, mathematics, business, creative arts, hospitality, tourism and social development.
